key_insight: Right ventricular trabeculation appears to be shaped by both shared cardiac biology and RV-specific developmental and cardiopulmonary genetic pathways.
clinical_relevance: RV trabecular complexity may become a useful biomarker for linking imaging features with cardiometabolic, respiratory, and congenital heart disease risk in large adult populations.
method: Deep-learning image segmentation quantified RV trabeculation on UK Biobank cardiac MRI.
Fractal dimension analysis measured trabecular complexity in both diastole and systole.
Genetic analyses mapped common loci and protein-altering variants across the allele frequency spectrum.
evidence_signal: The study analyzed 48,118 UK Biobank participants with genetic data and identified 52 common loci plus 45 genes with burden signals associated with RV trabeculation.
watch_item: Findings are associative and based on one large cohort, so clinical implementation would require external validation and longitudinal testing.
paper_title: Genetic regulation of right ventricular trabeculation identifies developmental and cardiopulmonary pathways
